title: Deliver durable callbacks to the owning Claude coordinator
objective: Close the backend half of the missing Claude coordinator callback transport without touching VS Code UI files. Terminal task events routed to provider=claude must resolve the exact repository/window/session owner, persist a compact versioned aiworkhub.claude_callback.v1 sideband envelope, support a repository-bound claude CLI --resume delivery mode, and record a genuine matching acknowledgment before marking delivered. Preserve durable pending delivery across reload, active turns, process crashes and temporary unavailability. B855 independently owns the extension-side panel capability binding.
acceptance: The current hard-coded live_claude_panel_wake_transport_unavailable path is replaced by capability-detected delivery with an explicit panel, CLI-resume, or unavailable mode.
The backend resolves provider=claude through the current repo_id, window identity and Claude session identity without cross-repository fallback and emits aiworkhub.claude_callback.v1.
A terminal task event is delivered exactly once logically: duplicate events are idempotent and delivered is written only after matching acknowledgment.
If the Claude coordinator has an active turn, the callback remains durable pending and is retried after idle without parallel-turn injection or dead-letter churn.
Window reload, extension-host restart and temporary Claude unavailability preserve the queue and resume delivery automatically.
Only task_id, terminal state, event_id/request_id and an instruction to inspect the trusted review queue reach Claude; worker output, prompts, secrets and arbitrary card text are never injected.
The backend status contract reports Claude callback mode, redacted bound session suffix, pending age, last delivery/deferral reason and health without exposing the full session ID.
An end-to-end test proves review_ready -> durable outbox -> Claude transport -> matching ack -> delivered using the selected repository database.
A capability-negative test proves that an unavailable panel API is never reported as panel-delivered and that an unavailable CLI remains pending rather than lost.
Existing Codex callback behavior and repository isolation remain unchanged.
